faq.q: Did a rule cut my price for the wedding weekend?
faq.a: One of your rules may have. Open the Change Log tab and find the night. Each change names the rule that acted and the reason, in one or two sentences. The change log only reaches back about 50 minutes. For an older change, check the night's Current price and any Manual badge on the calendar, and email us the night and room type: the detail behind every change is kept for 90 days, and we can read it for you. If a booking speed rule cut the night, the sentence reads something like "Bookings came in much slower than normal this past month: 1, against the 5 a night like this usually has by now."

faq.q: Why did nothing change today?
faq.a: Most pricing runs change nothing, and the change log hides them by default. Press Show All Cycles and each stretch of those runs shows as one line, such as "Prices checked 47 times from Sep 24, 10:05 AM to 1:55 PM (4 min ago), nothing needed to change." A quiet property is a property whose rules were checked and found no reason to act.

faq.q: Can I undo that?
faq.a: Yes, three ways, and one that does not work.

faq.q: Is it sending prices right now?
faq.a: MAYA sends prices only when you have gone live, and only for nights whose price changed since the last send. There is no "sending" light on the dashboard, and no badge that says live or simulation. The word live beside the time at the top right of the calendar ("Updated 3:05:12 PM · live") only means the calendar refreshes by itself. It shows in simulation too. Here is how to tell.

faq.q: Why did the price jump 50%?
faq.a: Two rules acted on the same night, and percentages compound. Standard rules (occupancy and booking window) apply first, then each booking speed or pickup fire in the order it was made, then the floor and ceiling. A +10% followed by a +25% is not +35%: $200 becomes $220, then $275.

faq.q: Why did a rule raise a night that is empty?
faq.a: Because booking speed compares a night with what similar past nights had received at the same point before arrival, not with how full it is. A night 50 days out is compared with how its similar nights were booking when they were 50 days out. If those nights had received none at all by then, 2 or 3 bookings in a week read Much Faster Than Normal, or Faster Than Normal when there are fewer than 5 similar nights to compare with. If they had averaged a fraction of a booking, 0.4 say, it takes 3, because a difference of less than 2 bookings always reads Normal.

faq.q: Why did it cut a night that is nearly full?
faq.a: A cut rule with only a booking speed condition does not look at occupancy. It counts bookings made in its window (past day, week or month, in full days up to yesterday) and compares them with similar nights over the same stretch. A night that filled up months ago and received one booking this month reads slower than a night like it usually books, and the cut fires.

faq.q: We are sold out tonight. Why is the price still changing?
faq.a: MAYA does not read how many rooms your system still has for sale. A full night is priced like any other: your rules run on it whenever its bookings change and once a day, and once you are live its price is sent whenever it changes (Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations). That is on purpose. A cancellation puts a room back on sale, and it sells at the rate your system has at that moment, which is MAYA's latest price once you are live.

faq.q: Why is a price at $1?
faq.a: That is the default floor, $1.00, and it stops nothing in practice. A cut rule that fires again after each wait, on a night that keeps reading slow, walks the price down until the floor catches it. With no floor set, the floor is $1.

faq.q: Why is a price at $99,999?
faq.a: That is the default ceiling, $99,999.99. In most currencies it has the same effect as no ceiling at all. Raise rules that keep firing on a night that keeps reading fast climb until the ceiling stops them.

faq.q: Why is my price stuck at the floor?
faq.a: Every published price is held between the room type's floor and ceiling. When the rules ask for less than the floor, the floor is published and the change log says "That would have dropped under your $80.00 floor for Standard, so it stopped there."

faq.q: Why did a price change with no rule named?
faq.a: Three shapes of entry have no rule name.

faq.q: Why did the price go back to the base rate?
faq.a: Four reasons, and the change log names each.

faq.q: Why is a night unpriced?

faq.q: Why did my rule fire three times and keep going?
faq.a: Because it keeps going until you answer. Once three of a booking speed or pickup rule's changes are on the same night, the amber Rules that keep adjusting banner appears at the top of every tab: ""Hot-week surge" has 3 raises on Fri, Nov 13 2026." and "It keeps raising these nights until you stop it."

faq.q: Why does the same rule appear twice on one night?
faq.a: ""Slow-date trim" lowered this night 7%, from $200.00 to $186.00." and, after its reason, "Then "Slow-date trim" lowered it another 7%, from $186.00 to $172.98." is one rule that fired, waited its wait, and fired again. A booking speed rule can act on the same night more than once. After the first change it counts only bookings made in the full days since the newest cut still on the night by itself or a stronger rule, up to yesterday, compared with similar nights over the same days, and if those still read slow it cuts again. Three of its changes on one night bring the amber banner.

faq.q: Why does it say Faster or Much Faster Than Normal from two bookings?
faq.a: Because the nights it was compared with had received almost none by that point. A night 50 days out is compared with how its similar nights were booking when they were 50 days out, which is often close to nothing. When the similar nights had received none at all, 2 or 3 bookings read Much Faster Than Normal and 4 or more read Surging, provided there are at least 5 similar nights. Against an expectation of 0.4, 2 bookings still read Normal: it takes 3 to read Much Faster and 5 to read Surging. One booking stays Normal against either, because a difference of one is inside the first check.

faq.q: Why does it say Normal when we got far more bookings than usual?
faq.a: One of the three checks kept the reading nearer Normal, and the Show the numbers panel names which:

faq.q: Why is it comparing my Friday with a Saturday?
faq.a: Because strict matching found too few nights. MAYA looks for similar nights in three widening steps: first the same weekday in the same stretch of the year, going back up to 3 years, wanting at least 4 and taking up to 8. When that finds too few, it widens to the same weekend or weekday class, day by day. Friday and Saturday nights form the weekend class, so a Friday can be matched with a Saturday. When that is still too few, it takes the same weekday within 45 days of the date, ignoring the season.

faq.q: Why did it compare with a festival weekend?
faq.a: Because nobody had told MAYA that weekend was unusual. Open the change, press Show the numbers, then Which nights were compared?, then List the nights. Beside the festival night press Not a fair comparison?, choose a reason such as Local Event or Festival, and press Set this date aside.

faq.q: Why was our national holiday not recognised?
faq.a: MAYA has 17 US holidays and no others, and there is no screen to add one. A night near one of those holidays is compared with the same position around the same holiday in earlier years. A night near any other holiday is compared like an ordinary night.

faq.q: Does a 10-room group count as 10 bookings?
faq.a: No. For booking speed a booking counts once, however many rooms it holds, on the night it is made and on every past night it is compared with. A 10-room group booked as one reservation is one booking. For occupancy it is 10 booked rooms. For a pickup count rule it is 10 room nights.

faq.q: Why did a Confirmation Pending booking count?
faq.a: On Cloudbeds, a booking with the status Confirmation Pending (Cloudbeds calls it not confirmed) holds a room, and Cloudbeds' own occupancy counts it as sold. MAYA counts it the same way, for occupancy and for booking speed. Cancelled bookings and no-shows do not count, and a booking that cancels disappears from the count on the next read.

faq.q: Why do Mews Optional reservations count?
faq.a: On Mews, every reservation counts except a cancelled one. Optional, Enquired and Requested reservations count as booked, for occupancy and for booking speed, exactly like a Confirmed one. On ThinkReservations every booking counts except cancelled bookings and no-shows.

faq.q: Why is the usual number a fraction like 0.4?
faq.a: Because it is an average. The usual number, the expected count, is the trimmed average of what the similar nights had received over the same stretch: a plain average with fewer than 5 nights, and with 5 or more the single highest and lowest are dropped first. An expected count of 0.4 is a true statement about a quiet far-out night: most similar nights had none, one or two had one. On screen it reads "almost no bookings" when it is under 1, and "about 3 bookings" otherwise. A similar night with no bookings at all in your history is left out of the average, not counted as zero.

faq.q: Do cancellations lower the count?
faq.a: Yes, but the count never goes below zero. It counts the bookings for the night that were made during the window and are still on the books. A booking that cancels drops out on the next read, so cancellations lower the count, down to none at the lowest. A booking made before the window that cancels during it was never in the count, so it changes nothing.

faq.q: Why does it say "in the 4 days since this rule or a stronger one's latest raise"?
faq.a: After a night has been raised, a rule that raises counts only the bookings made from the newest raise still on that night by itself or by a stronger rule, a rule you have switched off included. A weaker rule's raise does not change where it counts from, and nor does a raise by a standard rule, one with only occupancy or booking window conditions. A raise that has come off no longer counts.

faq.q: Why did a booking speed rule fire on a room type with no bookings?
faq.a: A rule reads bookings across every room type it measures, then changes every room type in its change list. "Hot-week surge" measuring Standard, Deluxe and Suite reads one count for all three. Six bookings on Standard and Deluxe against an expectation of 2 read Much Faster, and the rule raises Suite too, with no Suite booking in sight.

faq.q: Why does MAYA's occupancy differ from Cloudbeds'?
faq.a: Two reasons. Both can make MAYA's number higher than Cloudbeds', and the second can also make it lower.

faq.q: Why is my occupancy wrong when rooms are out of order?
faq.a: Because nobody has told MAYA. Rooms out of order in your property system are not read. Enter them in MAYA: on the PMS tab, under the room type, press + Rooms out of service, fill in From, To, Units and an optional Reason (optional), and press Save. Those rooms come off the sellable count for those nights only, and your rules run on those nights again from the next cycle if they fall within the 396-night window. Nothing is sent to your property system about the block.

faq.q: Why is occupancy over 100%?
faq.a: Because more rooms are booked than MAYA reads as sellable. It happens when you mark rooms out of service after they were already sold (12 rooms, 3 out of service, 10 booked reads 111%), or when your property system has overbooked the night. MAYA does not cap the number.

faq.q: Why is my occupancy tiny on ThinkReservations or Mews?
faq.a: On Mews, every room category Mews sends no room count for gets the same number of rooms, one number for your whole property, 100 until we change it. A category with 6 rooms and 5 booked reads 5% instead of 83%, and occupancy rules that need a full night never fire.

faq.q: Why does a room type show 100 rooms?
faq.a: The PMS tab's Room types list shows "100 units" for a room type whose room count MAYA does not have. On Cloudbeds the count is read from your system on every cycle, so this is rare and means Cloudbeds reported none. On ThinkReservations it is read from your list of rooms on every cycle, so it shows only when MAYA could not read that list when the room type first appeared, and the next cycle that reads the list puts the real count in. On Mews it is every room category Mews sends no room count for, until we set the one number for your property: email us the real count.

faq.q: Does a group of 10 count as 10 rooms?
faq.a: Yes, for occupancy. A booking that holds 10 rooms is 10 booked rooms on each of its nights. That is different from booking speed, where a booking counts once however many rooms it holds. Read Booking speed reads oddly.

faq.q: Why does day revenue include my meeting room?
faq.a: The day card's revenue figure sums every room type, including ones you have unticked as rooms. Occupancy and the "12/20 rooms" line use only the ticked ones. So a meeting room booking adds to revenue and not to occupancy.

faq.q: Why does day revenue differ from a revenue pickup rule?
faq.a: They value a booked night differently. The day card values each booked night at the booking's rate as it was imported, falling back to its current rate, and at 0 when neither is on file. A pickup count rule set to Revenue (currency) sums each booked night's current rate as your system reports it. The two can differ for the same night. Neither figure is sent anywhere.

faq.q: Why does day revenue not match my property system's revenue report?
faq.a: MAYA adds up the nightly rates your system reports for booked nights. It never adds tax or takes off a booking site's commission, and what the rate includes depends on your system: in Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations it is the room rate on the same basis as your own rates, and in Mews it is the booking total, taxes included, split across its nights. A report that adds taxes, fees or extras, or takes off commission, will differ. The calendar has the detail for each system.

faq.q: Why did MAYA price a night I closed in my system?

faq.q: Why was a night I set to 0 not sent?
faq.a: MAYA does not send a price of 0 to any property system. A manual price of 0 is a comp night: no rule raises it, and the save confirmation says "Saved. MAYA doesn't send a price of 0 to Cloudbeds, so set the night to 0 there yourself." The change log carries an item that says the same until your system has the night at 0. Set it there yourself. faq.q: Why was a night 70 days out not sent?
faq.a: MAYA prices and sends tonight and the next 395 nights, on your property's own calendar. A night 70 days out is not priced, refreshed or sent until it enters the window. A manual price you type further out is saved now and sent when the night enters the window, and the confirmation says so: "Saved. It will be sent when the date enters the 396-day push window."

faq.q: Why did MAYA disconnect after my Cloudbeds subscription changed?
faq.a: When Cloudbeds answers with its wording for an app that is no longer connected, MAYA marks the connection disconnected at once and shows the banner. A change to your Cloudbeds subscription or apps can cause that. Reconnect as above. If a change to your Cloudbeds login stops the connection, the same banner appears and Reconnect Cloudbeds fixes it.

faq.q: ThinkReservations lost its connection, how would I tell?
faq.a: MAYA shows the banner and the Reconnect Think Reservations button when the connection stops working and its status changes. Because ThinkReservations does not tell MAYA, that can lag: MAYA's reads fail first and are retried with a growing gap of up to an hour, and the banner follows once the status is marked. If Last sync on the PMS tab is hours old and no banner shows, press Reconnect Think Reservations there anyway, with a login for this hotel only. It is harmless on a working connection.

faq.q: Will I get an email?
faq.a: Yes, once the connection has read Error or Disconnected for about an hour. Every General Manager and Hotel Admin on the property gets one email, headed "MAYA has lost its connection to Cloudbeds" (or your system), saying when it went down, what happened, what it means for your prices and how to reconnect. Its button, Open the PMS tab, opens the tab where you reconnect. On Mews, reply to it and we arrange new keys with you.

faq.q: Why is "Last sync" old?
faq.a: Last sync is the last time bookings were read successfully. On a healthy connection it is a few minutes old. After a failed read MAYA waits longer before each retry, doubling each time up to an hour, so a system that is down for a while leaves Last sync up to an hour behind before it catches up. A disconnected property stops reading altogether until someone reconnects. A paused subscription stops it too.

faq.q: Why does Health say "Having trouble"?
faq.a: Health (last 24 hours) counts MAYA's requests to your system over the last day: "Healthy" when 98% or more succeeded, "Degraded" from 80%, "Having trouble" below that, with the figure beside it, for example "76% of 412 requests OK". "Having trouble" usually means your system was down or refusing for part of the day. If the connection card reads Connected and Last sync is recent, the trouble has passed. If not, reconnect.

faq.q: After reconnecting, how do I know it worked?
faq.a: A successful reconnect brings you back to the dashboard's PMS tab, on the property you reconnected, with a short note: "Reconnected." Close it with the ×. The banner stops showing once the connection reads Connected, and a few minutes later Last sync shows a fresh time.

faq.q: What happens to my prices while the connection is down?
faq.a: Nothing is read, priced or sent. The rates already in your system stay exactly as they are. After you reconnect, the next cycle reads your bookings, prices again and sends what changed. Any price held back by a permission problem goes out then too.

faq.q: Why is every day amber?
faq.a: Colours need something to compare with. Each night's room revenue is divided by the property's room count to give revenue per room, and past nights are ranked against your other past nights, future nights against your other future nights. With fewer than 10 nights on a side, MAYA borrows both sides together, and with fewer than 10 in total there is no scale and every night is amber. A new property, or a property whose history is still importing, is amber until it has enough nights. The legend under the grid says "measured by revenue per room, relative to this property's own results".

faq.q: Why is a busy night red?
faq.a: Because the colour is revenue per room, not occupancy. A full night at low rates can earn less per room than a half-full night at high rates. Red is the bottom third of your nights, amber the middle third, green the top third, each side (past, future) ranked on its own. The colour tells you how the night's revenue ranks against your own nights, and nothing else.

faq.q: Why did the colour not change after a booking?
faq.a: The booked counts and revenue on the visible month are always fresh, but the ranking they are coloured against is kept for up to 5 minutes. A colour can lag a new booking by that long. The calendar also refreshes itself every 5 minutes on the Calendar tab and when you return to the browser tab.

faq.q: Why does the calendar show $ when my currency is euro?
faq.a: The calendar shows the sign of the currency saved for your property: $ for US dollars, € for euros, £ for pounds, and the three-letter code in front of the amount for any other currency. So do the manual price box and its Manual badge, the Rate Simulator, the sentences under each change, the amber alert banner and the manual price error messages. If the calendar shows $ and your property is in euros, MAYA has US dollars saved for it. That is what a property gets when its currency was not read from its system when it connected. Check Time zone and currency on the PMS tab, and email us to correct it.

faq.q: Why does ADR show a dash when nothing is booked?
faq.a: The room type card's ADR (average daily rate: that night's room revenue divided by the rooms booked) needs at least one booking. When Booked reads 0 there is nothing to average, so the line reads "ADR –". Look at Current price for the price your rules have set.

faq.q: Why does today say "revenue" instead of "revenue on the books"?
faq.a: The day detail reads "revenue on the books" for today and later, and "revenue" for past days. At properties in the Americas, today's heading can switch from "revenue on the books" to "revenue" in the evening. It is only a label and changes no price. Pricing always uses your property's own date.

faq.q: Why are there no weekday headers?
faq.a: The month grid has none. Click a day and its heading names the weekday: "Friday, November 13, 2026". The grid starts on Sunday.

faq.q: Why do past months show zeros?
faq.a: Nights before your property's imported history have nothing to show. The year picker runs from the first month with a booking or a price to the last.

faq.q: Why are there so many "Prices checked" entries?
faq.a: Pressing Show All Cycles adds the quiet lines, and a run happens about every five minutes whenever bookings were read. Each line counts a stretch of runs that changed nothing: "Prices checked 47 times from Sep 24, 10:05 AM to 1:55 PM, nothing needed to change." That is MAYA checking your rules and finding no reason to act. Press Show Changes Only to go back to the default view, which keeps only runs that changed something, sending problems and your answers.

faq.q: Why is the change log empty?
faq.a: Simulation is not a reason: while simulating, every run happens and is written down.

faq.q: Why did an older change disappear?
faq.a: The change log holds the 10 most recent runs that changed a price, with the quiet runs between them counted into lines. An older run drops off the bottom as new changes arrive, so on a busy day a change from this morning may already be gone.

faq.q: Why are only some of a run's changes listed?
faq.a: A run lists its 40 biggest moves, largest percentage first. A run that changed more nights than that shows 40, then a line counting the rest, such as "And 23 more changes in this run." In a very large run the count can be a minimum: "And at least 23 more changes in this run." The rest are not listed anywhere in the app. To see where a night stands now, open it on the Calendar tab.

faq.q: Why is "Show the numbers" missing on some changes?
faq.a: The button appears under a change when the run that made it also took a booking speed reading for that night. While any rule you have switched on uses booking speed (every booking speed starter rule does), each run takes that reading on nearly every night in the window. So the button shows under most changes, including ones made by an occupancy or booking window rule, a price you typed, or a rate changed in your system.

faq.q: Whose time zone are the log times in?
faq.a: Your browser's. "Pricing run · Fri, Sep 18, 2026, 3:05 PM PDT" is the time on your computer's clock, with its zone abbreviation. Hover the time for the exact moment, to the second, on the same clock. Last sync and the request times on the PMS tab use your clock too. Pricing itself works in your property's own time zone, and the "Updated 3:05:12 PM · live" time on the calendar is also your browser's clock.

faq.q: Why does the PMS tab say "Not tracked for this system" on ThinkReservations or Mews?
faq.a: The Health (last 24 hours) card and the Recent requests table are filled from a log of MAYA's requests, and MAYA keeps that log for Cloudbeds only. On a ThinkReservations or Mews property both read "Not tracked for this system", however healthy the connection is. Use Connection and Last sync on those properties instead.

faq.q: A colleague already signed up for our property, how do I get in?
faq.a: They invite you. On the Team page they enter your email, pick your role and press Send invitation. You get an email with a link to set a password and join. If you have signed in to MAYA before, you are added at once with no email, and the property appears the next time you open MAYA. Read Inviting and removing people.

faq.q: Why did signing in take me to a payment page?
faq.a: Because a property attached to your account is connected but not paid for. A Cloudbeds Marketplace property is connected first and paid for second, so until payment is set up, signing in lands on the subscribe screen. Set up payment, or press "Not now" if it is one of several properties and you want to come back to it. Read Setting up payment.

faq.q: Why did the dashboard send me to onboarding?
faq.a: Your account has no property that is set up and active yet. Onboarding is where you pay, connect and review. If a colleague has the property, ask them to invite you.

faq.q: Was I charged twice?
faq.a: No. MAYA checks your saved card twice with a zero-amount check that moves no money: once right after checkout, and again 48 hours after the subscription starts. Some banks briefly show a pending line that then disappears. It is never charged. The receipt for a real charge comes from Stripe.

faq.q: Why is the next charge different from the calculator?
faq.a: The billing page shows Stripe's own preview of your next invoice, which includes any code you used and, where it applies, tax. The calculator on the website shows the list price for your room count. The two agree once a discount ends. Read The billing page.

faq.q: Why can't I see the billing page?
faq.a: It needs General Manager or Hotel Admin access. Anyone else sees "Billing is handled by this property's General Manager or Hotel Admin. Ask one of them for access if you need to change it." The Team page works the same way. Read Roles.

faq.q: Why is my property missing from the dropdown?
faq.a: The Property dropdown lists only properties you belong to that are paid for and set up. A property you set aside with "Not now" during a group setup is listed on the billing page under Properties not set up yet, where Set up takes you back to pay for it. A property someone else owns needs an invitation from them.
